# CoolROM

> CoolROM (coolrom.com) has been a retro gaming resource since 2002: game files (ROMs and disc images) for classic consoles, handhelds and arcade systems, the emulators that play them, the BIOS files some systems need, and a guide to putting them together.

The site is organised by system. Each system has an A–Z list of its games, genre lists, and its most downloaded and best rated games. Each game has its own page with screenshots, the file's name and size, visitors' ratings and a download button. The interface is available in 24 languages, and the same pages adapt to phones and tablets.

Download links are made for the visitor who opens the page and expire, so link to a game's page rather than to a file.

## Main sections

- [ROMs and ISOs by system](https://coolrom.com/roms/): every system and its games
- [Emulators](https://coolrom.com/emulators/): emulators for Windows, Mac, Android and iOS, by system
- [BIOS files](https://coolrom.com/bios/): the BIOS files some emulators need
- [Getting started](https://coolrom.com/tutorial.php): how to download a game, unpack it and play it in an emulator
- [FAQ](https://coolrom.com/faq.php): common questions about the site
- [Search](https://coolrom.com/search): find a game by its name

## Optional

- [Privacy policy](https://coolrom.com/privacy.php)
- [Contact](https://coolrom.com/contact.php)

<meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1">
<style type="text/css">
/* The phone bar (cr_resp_bar() below) is hidden here and shown inside the media query: by this stylesheet, which is
   in <head>, so it is right from the first paint, with no script and no flash on a desktop window. It used to be
   display:none inline and shown by its script -- which Cloudflare's Rocket Loader runs only once the page has loaded:
   the bar, and the logo in it, appeared seconds late (the logo is the download page's largest element: PageSpeed's
   LCP 5-6 s there) and pushed the page down when they did (CLS up to 0.135 on a game page). 6 Nov 2026. */
#crmb-wrap{display:none}
/* The phone spelling of a fold label (crb-flong / crb-fshort, browse_head.php),
   hidden here and shown inside the media query -- by this stylesheet, for the same
   reason as the bar above, and for one more: roms.php includes header.php (which
   brings this file in) at line 1590 and includes/browse_styles.php at 1617, so
   browse_styles.php is emitted AFTER this one. A default of the same specificity
   placed there wins on source order and the media query below never takes effect --
   which hid BOTH spellings and left three pills showing nothing but their carets.
   Same trap as emulator_styles.php, which is emitted after this file too. */
#crb .crb-fshort{display:none}
/* The phone spelling of the copyright line (footer.php), hidden here for the same reason and by the same
   stylesheet as the bar above: it is in <head>, so it is right from the first paint. */
.ftr-short{display:none}
@media screen and (max-width:700px),
       screen and (max-width:1000px) and (max-height:480px) and (orientation:landscape){

/* ---- no double-tap zoom on things you tap ----------------------------------
   Tapping the hamburger twice in quick succession zoomed the page instead of
   opening and closing the menu: the browser waits to see whether a second tap
   is coming, and a second tap on the same spot is the double-tap-to-zoom
   gesture. The menu is the obvious victim, but it applies to anything people
   tap twice -- the Go button, a filter chip, a download button.

   touch-action:manipulation tells the browser this element never needs that
   gesture. Panning and PINCH zoom still work, so the page can still be zoomed
   deliberately; only the double-tap shortcut is off, and only on controls. It
   also removes the ~300ms wait before the tap registers, since there is no
   longer a second tap to wait for, which makes the whole layout feel quicker.

   Not done with user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 on the viewport meta: that
   would kill pinch zoom for everyone, including anyone who needs it to read the
   page, and iOS has ignored it since iOS 10 anyway. */
a,button,input,select,summary,label,.crs-chip,.crb-toggle a
	{touch-action:manipulation}

/* iOS inflates text on its own when it decides a block is too wide to read, and
   it leaves form controls out of that. On the desktop layout seen from a phone
   that is why the navbar's <a> links came out bigger than the Emulators and ROMs
   <button> dropdowns beside them, in Portuguese and in every other language --
   the CSS gives all seven bold 13px, and a desktop browser renders them that way.
   Sizes here are chosen for the screen they are on, so the inflation is off. */
html{-webkit-text-size-adjust:100%;text-size-adjust:100%}

/* ---- the shell ------------------------------------------------------------
   The page frame is a fixed 980px two-column table (main + rail). Rather than
   rewrite markup that sits on every page, the cells are told to stack:
   display:block drops the table formatting and the two columns become two
   rows. The colgroup must go with them or its declared 644px/336px widths
   carry on applying to the first two blocks. */
table.crmb-outer,table.crmb-outer>tbody,table.crmb-outer>tbody>tr,table.crmb-outer>tbody>tr>td,
table.crmb-shell,table.crmb-shell>tbody,table.crmb-shell>tbody>tr,table.crmb-shell>tbody>tr>td,
table.crmb-wide,table.crmb-wide>tbody,table.crmb-wide>tbody>tr,table.crmb-wide>tbody>tr>td
	{display:block;width:auto !important;height:auto !important}
table.crmb-shell>colgroup{display:none}
table.crmb-wide>tbody>tr>td{text-align:left !important}

/* Content tables still carry width="528" / "450" / "300" attributes from the
   fixed-width era (roms.php, roms2.php, bios.php, emulators.php). An attribute
   width is a used width, not a cap, so inside a ~390px column they push the
   page sideways. max-width lets them shrink and their cells wrap. */
table{max-width:100%}
img{max-width:100%;height:auto}

/* The rail is hidden for now (owner, 4 Nov 2026): stacked below the content
   its 300x250 sat far under the fold and the lists made every page very long.
   The CELL goes, not just #crr, so its background and left border go too.
   width="336" identifies it, footer.php having no class to target. */
table.crmb-shell>tbody>tr>td[width="336"]{display:none}

/* ---- the desktop header, hidden ------------------------------------------
   The logo row carries the logo, the bookmark line and the translate form; the
   navbar row carries the link list and the search box. Both are replaced by
   #crmb-bar below. .crmb-hide is put on them by header.php, on this host only. */
.crmb-hide{display:none !important}

/* ---- the mobile header ----------------------------------------------------
   Logo left, burger right, search across the full width underneath. Shown here, by the media query (see the top). */
#crmb-wrap{display:block}
/* 4px top and bottom, not 8. The bar is 50px tall and must stay that way -- anything else pushes
   the whole page down -- so the padding and the logo's height below trade against each other:
   4 + 42 + 4 is the same 50 as 8 + 34 + 8 was (the owner, 7 Nov 2026). Change one, change the other.
   The burger does not move whatever split is chosen: it is a fixed 34px centred in the row, so it
   always ends up 8px from each edge of the bar. Measured at every step from 34/8 to 46/2. */
/* The blue rule along the bottom is an INSET shadow, not a border: a border would sit outside the
   50px this bar is held to and push the whole page down by 2px, which is exactly what the note
   above forbids. An inset shadow paints within the box and costs no layout at all (Ed, 16 Nov 2026). */
#crmb-bar{background:#000;padding:4px 10px 4px 5px;display:flex;align-items:center;gap:8px;
	box-shadow:inset 0 -2px 0 #4276bc}
/* flex:0 1 auto with an auto right margin, not flex:1 1 auto (Ed, 16 Nov 2026). Growing the anchor
   made it fill every pixel between the logo and the buttons, so a tap anywhere in that empty black
   stretch went to the home page. Now the anchor is only as wide as the artwork and the free space
   lives in a margin, which nothing can click -- the buttons stay hard right exactly as before.
   min-width:0 is kept so the logo still gives way first if a narrow screen ever runs out of room. */
#crmb-bar .crmb-logo{flex:0 1 auto;min-width:0;margin-right:auto;line-height:0}
/* Sized by HEIGHT, which is now what sets the row: 42px, taller than the burger's 34px, with the
   bar's vertical padding cut to 4px to pay for it (see above). The gap under the logo is that 4px.
   width:auto keeps the 291x66 ratio, so this lands at 185px wide -- the logo cannot be made taller
   without also being wider, that is the trade.
   It was sized by width before, at 136px, which came out 30.84px tall and floated 3px short of the
   square; driving it off height is what stops the two drifting apart (the owner, 7 Nov 2026).
   The bar's left gutter stays halved to 5px in the padding above, so it still starts near the edge. */
/* max-width and object-fit added with the account button (Ed, 18 Nov 2026). A third 40px control plus its
   8px gap is 48px the bar did not have: at 320px the row is 305px wide inside its padding, three buttons and
   three gaps take 144 of it, and 161 is left for a logo whose natural width at this height is 185. Without
   these two the image simply overflowed the bar. contain scales it down inside whatever is left and keeps the
   291x66 ratio, so the row's height never moves and a wide phone still gets the logo at full size. */
#crmb-bar .crmb-logo img{width:auto;height:42px;max-width:100%;object-fit:contain;
	object-position:left center;border:0;display:block}
/* The two buttons in the bar: search, then the burger (Ed, 16 Nov 2026). Both are grey while they
   are shut and take the bar's blue once they are open, so the bar reads as quiet until something is
   actually expanded. aria-expanded is the only switch -- the script already keeps it truthful, so
   there is no second class to go stale, and a screen reader and the paint can never disagree.
   Both stay 40x34, which is what holds the bar at the 50px the note above insists on: a second
   button adds 48px of WIDTH (40 + the 8px gap) and no height at all. At 320px the bar then needs
   296px of its 320, and the logo is flex:1 1 auto with min-width:0, so it gives way first. */
/* No fill and no visible edge at rest: a filled button that barely differs from the black behind it
   is neither quiet nor clear, and it read as an empty slot rather than a control. The border is kept
   at 1px TRANSPARENT rather than removed, so gaining its colour when the button opens cannot nudge
   the 40x34 box by the 2px a border would otherwise add. */
#crmb-search,#crmb-burger,#crmb-queue{flex:0 0 auto;width:40px;height:34px;background:none;
	border:1px solid transparent;border-radius:4px;cursor:pointer}
#crmb-burger{padding:8px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;justify-content:space-between}
#crmb-burger span{display:block;height:2px;background:#79b4ef;border-radius:2px}
#crmb-search,#crmb-queue{padding:0;display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;color:#79b4ef}
/* An <a>, not a button: it goes somewhere rather than opening something, so it has no aria-expanded and
   needs its own text-decoration reset -- the bar's other two are <button> and never had one. */
#crmb-queue{text-decoration:none;position:relative}
/* The count rides the icon's top-right corner. min-width rather than width so three digits still fit --
   the queue stops at 100 -- and the pill grows sideways instead of clipping. */
#crmb-queue .crmb-qn{position:absolute;top:1px;right:1px;min-width:15px;height:15px;box-sizing:border-box;
	padding:0 3px;border-radius:8px;background:#4276bc;border:1px solid #0d0d0d;
	color:#fff;font:bold 9.5px/13px Verdana,Arial;text-align:center}
/* currentColor, so the one colour rule below moves the glass and the handle together. */
/* 24px, up from 18 (Ed, 18 Nov 2026). At 18 these read as smaller and lighter than the burger beside them,
   and the stroke was why: both glyphs are drawn in a 24-unit viewBox with stroke-width:2, so at 18px the line
   came out at 1.5px against the burger's 2px bars. Drawn at 24 the stroke is exactly 2px and the glyphs span
   the same 22px the burger's bars do -- the three controls now match in weight as well as in box size. The
   button stays 40x34, so a 24px glyph still has 5px of air above and below and the row height does not move. */
#crmb-search svg,#crmb-queue svg{display:block;width:24px;height:24px;fill:none;stroke:currentColor;
	stroke-width:2;stroke-linecap:round}
/* Open: #4276bc with the #79b4ef edge -- the same pair the panel and the menu already use. */
#crmb-search[aria-expanded="true"],#crmb-burger[aria-expanded="true"]{background:#4276bc;border-color:#79b4ef}
#crmb-search[aria-expanded="true"]{color:#fff}
#crmb-burger[aria-expanded="true"] span{background:#fff}
/* Hover only where there IS a hover (Ed, 16 Nov 2026). A touch screen leaves :hover stuck on the
   last thing tapped until something else is tapped, so after closing a panel the button it was
   closed with kept its grey fill and read as still open. (hover:hover) is false on a phone, so the
   fill never applies there and the only fill the button ever shows there is the blue of being open.
   -webkit-tap-highlight-color kills the separate grey flash iOS paints over a tapped control. */
#crmb-search,#crmb-burger,#crmb-queue{-webkit-tap-highlight-color:transparent}
/* ...and on everything in the bar, not only the three controls (Ed, 18 Nov 2026). The flash is painted on
   whichever ancestor the browser decides is clickable, so setting it on the button alone still let the row
   around it light up when the search icon was tapped. The descendant selector costs nothing here -- it is a
   bar with five elements in it -- and it covers the search row that appears underneath as well.
   user-select with it: a tap that the browser reads as the start of a drag otherwise selects the text either
   side of the icon, which is the other way that row ends up highlighted. The input is exempted below, or the
   visitor could not select what they had typed. */
#crmb-wrap,#crmb-wrap *{-webkit-tap-highlight-color:transparent}
#crmb-search,#crmb-burger,#crmb-queue,#crmb-bar .crmb-logo{
	-webkit-user-select:none;-moz-user-select:none;-ms-user-select:none;user-select:none}
#crmb-find input[type=text]{-webkit-user-select:text;user-select:text}
@media (hover:hover){
	#crmb-search:hover,#crmb-burger:hover,#crmb-queue:hover{background:#1f1f1f}
	/* #5685c4 on hover over the #4276bc above -- header.php's pair again. #4e97db was a third
	   blue doing the same job, and the weakest of them against white at 3.10:1. */
	#crmb-search[aria-expanded="true"]:hover,
	#crmb-burger[aria-expanded="true"]:hover{background:#5685c4;border-color:#aed3f7}
}
#crmb-search:focus-visible,#crmb-burger:focus-visible,#crmb-menu a:focus-visible,
#crmb-menu .crmb-sub:focus-visible{outline:2px solid #fff;outline-offset:-2px}

/* The search box sits AFTER the menu in the source, so opening the menu pushes it
   down the page instead of the menu unrolling underneath it. */
/* #262626, not the black above it (the owner, 7 Nov 2026 -- "the same color as the body grey").
   That is the grey the page itself sits on: header.php's main content cell is
   <td bgcolor="#262626"> and it wraps <div role="main">, so this row reads as the top of the
   CONTENT rather than as more of the logo bar, and it is the same grey the desktop .search field
   uses. Padding left alone deliberately -- adding a top gap here would push every page down by
   that much, and the bar above was just balanced to hold its 50px. */
#crmb-find{display:flex;margin:0;background:#262626;padding:0 10px 8px}
/* Spelled out, because the id selector above outranks the browser's own [hidden] rule and the
   field would otherwise stay on screen with the attribute set (Ed, 16 Nov 2026). */
#crmb-find[hidden]{display:none}

/* 3px over the first line of the page (Ed, 16 Nov 2026). The search row used to sit between the bar
   and the content and carried an 8px foot; with it shut by default the breadcrumb starts hard up
   against the bar. padding and not margin, so it cannot collapse into anything above it, and plain
   class selectors are enough -- every #cr? .cr?-crumb rule sets colour and margin only, never
   padding, so there is nothing here to outrank. All six pages carry a crumb of their own name. */
.crb-crumb,.crc-crumb,.crd-crumb,.cre-crumb,.crp-crumb,.crx-crumb{padding-top:3px}
/* 16px, not 14 (the owner, 6 Nov 2026). Under 16px iOS Safari zooms the whole page
   in when the field takes focus, and it does NOT zoom back out when the keyboard
   goes away -- the visitor is left on a magnified page to pinch out of. 16 is the
   threshold, so this is the whole fix. Android does not do it at all.
   Not user-scalable=no or maximum-scale=1 on the viewport meta: see the note on
   touch-action above for why that is the wrong lever.
   The cost is 2px: the bar measures 46px instead of 44, the field stays 324px wide
   at 390px and the GO button is untouched.
   The search PAGE's own box (.crs-q, 13px) would trip the same rule, but it never
   shows on a phone -- .crs-bar is display:none further down this file and this bar
   serves both. */
#crmb-find input[type=text]{flex:1 1 auto;min-width:0;font:16px Verdana,Arial;
	padding:9px 11px;background:#fff;border:1px solid #79b4ef;color:#222;
	box-sizing:border-box;border-radius:3px 0 0 3px}
/* No focus ring around the bar when the icon opens it (Ed, 20 Nov 2026). The field is focused by
   script the instant the panel slides out -- the tap was to search, not to look at a box -- and iOS
   draws its ring around a control focused that way, which here reads as one outline wrapping the
   field and GO together. The ring is doing no work: the bar has just appeared, the keyboard is up and
   the caret is in the field, so where focus went is not in question.
   The field keeps a focus state of its own, a lighter border, so this is a swap and not a removal --
   anyone arriving on it with a keyboard still sees it change. GO keeps its own ring untouched, for
   the same reason. */
#crmb-find:focus,#crmb-find:focus-visible{outline:0}
#crmb-find input[type=text]:focus{outline:0;border-color:#b8dcff}
#crmb-find button[type=submit]{flex:0 0 auto;font:bold 12px Verdana,Arial;
	padding:9px 16px;background:#4276bc;border:1px solid #79b4ef;border-left:0;
	color:#fff;text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.4px;cursor:pointer;
	border-radius:0 3px 3px 0}

/* The panel takes the burger's blue, with white text and white carets. */
/* margin-bottom, not padding on the search box: a hidden element has no margin,
   so the gap appears only while the menu is open. */
#crmb-menu{background:#4276bc;border-top:1px solid #79b4ef;margin-bottom:8px}
#crmb-menu a{display:block;padding:11px 14px;font:bold 13px Verdana,Arial;
	color:#fff !important;text-decoration:none;border-bottom:1px solid #6d99cf}
#crmb-menu a:hover{background:#5685c4;color:#fff !important}
/* The account row says WHO you are (Ed, 24 Nov 2026): "My Account - Username (Premium)".
   The name is the part that gets the ellipsis, because it is the part that can be arbitrarily long: for a
   member created by a Stripe checkout who has not chosen a username yet, cr_member_name() falls back to
   their EMAIL ADDRESS. The label and the status either side of it never shrink.
   min-width:0 on the name is what makes the ellipsis work at all -- a flex item will not shrink below its
   content's width without it, so the row would simply overflow the screen instead. Same rule the download
   panel's filename needed.
   The name is normal weight against the bold label: "My Account" is the link, the name is who is signed in,
   and at 13px bold a long address next to a bold label reads as one shouted string. */
#crmb-menu a.crmb-acct{display:flex;align-items:baseline;gap:5px}
/* flex:0 0 auto on the label and the separator, or they shrink too: every flex item shrinks by default, so a
   long address made "My Account" itself wrap onto two lines. Only the name may give way. */
/* · and not • (Ed, 24 Nov 2026): the bullet was too heavy between two words. Measured in Verdana
   on the owner's machine rather than guessed at -- bold 13px draws the bullet as 8x6px of ink and the middle
   dot as 4x2, so this is a real drop in weight and not a different-looking character of the same size.
   NOT a shrunken bullet: a smaller font-size on this span was tried and the dot fell towards the baseline,
   because the row is align-items:baseline and a bullet rides high in its own em. The middle dot sits at the
   right height at full size, so nothing else has to move. */
#crmb-menu .crmb-acct-lbl,
#crmb-menu .crmb-acct-dot{flex:0 0 auto}
#crmb-menu .crmb-acct-name{min-width:0;overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis;white-space:nowrap;
	font-weight:normal}
/* #ffd9a0, not the #df9e59 the desktop welcome bar uses. On this blue that one measures 2.02:1, which is
   unreadable; this is 3.45:1. Nothing in the orange family reaches the 4.5:1 a 13px bold label is supposed
   to have -- white itself only manages 4.62 here and 3.79 over the hover -- so this is the most legible
   orange available on #4276bc rather than a passing one. A dark chip behind it would reach 7.7:1 if the
   contrast ever has to be defensible. */
#crmb-menu .crmb-acct-prem{flex:0 0 auto;color:#ffd9a0}
#crmb-menu .crmb-sub{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:space-between;
	width:100%;box-sizing:border-box;padding:11px 14px;background:none;border:0;
	border-bottom:1px solid #6d99cf;font:bold 13px Verdana,Arial;color:#fff;
	cursor:pointer;text-align:left}
#crmb-menu .crmb-sub:hover{background:#5685c4}
#crmb-menu .crmb-sub .crmb-caret{font-size:10px;color:#fff;transition:transform .15s}
#crmb-menu .crmb-sub[aria-expanded="true"] .crmb-caret{transform:rotate(180deg)}
/* The expanded list is dark, not blue. With the systems open, a blue submenu on a
   blue menu filled the whole screen with one colour and nothing told you which
   rows were the nav and which were its contents. Dark does both jobs: far less
   blue, and the hierarchy reads at a glance. */
/* 58dvh after 58vh, not instead of it (the owner, 6 Nov 2026). On iOS Safari a vh is
   the LARGE viewport -- the height with the address bar retracted -- so a scroll box
   sized in vh is about 100px taller than what is actually on screen, and its last
   rows sit under the floating bar with no way to reach them. dvh is the viewport as
   it is right now, address bar and all, and it reflows when the bar comes and goes.
   Both lines on purpose: a browser that does not know dvh ignores the second and
   keeps the vh above, which is what it had before. */
/* 46 (Ed, 20 Nov 2026), and the number moved three times in one afternoon because the menu kept

/* The interstitial. Constraining #modal alone was not enough: it is centred with

#modal-background{overflow-y:auto}
/* 95% of the viewport, not a flat 10px gutter either side (the owner, 7 Nov 2026). The old pinning

#crHero h1{font-size:23px !important}

#crHero .crHeroSys a{font:bold 11px Verdana,Arial !important;
	padding:5px 8px !important;margin:0 2px !important}
#crHero p.crHeroSub{font-size:13px !important;line-height:1.55 !important}
/* padding-top/bottom come with the field's 16px above: the two are a joined control

#crHero input.crHeroGo{padding-left:12px !important;padding-right:12px !important;

	font-size:12px !important}
/* Featured games: all eight in one row that scrolls sideways. 104px cards put
   three on screen and leave about 45px of the fourth showing, which is the whole
   point -- a cut-off card is what tells you to swipe. Fixed px, not a percentage:
   the cells sit in an auto-layout table whose own width is indefinite, so a
   percentage there resolves against nothing. browse_styles.php pins the card to

#crb .crb-feat{overflow-x:auto;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch}
/* roms.php emits the eight cards as two table rows of four, which is what the
   desktop layout wants. A phone wants one row that scrolls sideways instead,
   and that regrouping happens here rather than in the PHP: emitting one long
   row for both builds is what made the strip overflow the 644px column in a

   the rows themselves out of the box tree and leaves their cards as the line's

#crb .crb-feat table,#crb .crb-feat tbody{display:block}

   ROM name can be one long unbroken string. Breaking it keeps the card 120px. */
#crb .crb-feat .crb-cap{overflow-wrap:break-word;word-wrap:break-word}
#crb .crb-feat .crb-card img{width:120px !important;height:auto !important;

#crb .crb-toggle{white-space:nowrap}
/* "TOP 50 DOWNLOADED" / "TOP 50 RATED": 11px, up from 10, which is what the
   desktop stylesheet uses. At 10 the two tabs were the smallest text on the
   browse page despite being the control that switches it. */
#crb .crb-toggle a{padding:4px 8px !important;font-size:11px !important;
	letter-spacing:0 !important}

/* --- browse page: controls sized for a finger ----------------------
   Measured on a 390px screen before this block, every control on the page
   was between 21px and 29px tall, and the A-Z chips were 19x23 -- against
   the 44px Apple and Google both give as the minimum for something you tap.
   They are that size because the desktop sheet fits 27 letters across a
   560px column in one unbroken strip, which is worth the small chips there.
   On a phone the alphabet already wraps to two lines, so that constraint is
   buying nothing and the chips can simply be bigger. */

/* Genre, region and the Top ROMs / View All pair. Width stays automatic, so
   a long translated genre still wraps inside the column as it does now.

   Sized down about 30% from the first pass (13px/9px/11px, 35px tall). Those were

#crb .crb-chip{font-size:11px !important;padding:5px 8px !important;
	margin:0 4px 4px 0 !important}


/* A-Z, brought down with the pills above: 11px type in a 24px chip, the same as
   the genre and region ones, so the whole filter block reads as one set of
   controls rather than two.

   The height and the type came down; the 37px WIDTH did not, and that is
   deliberate. These chips are inline-block, so how many land on a row is whatever
   fits -- and the width is the only thing setting it. At 37 a 390px screen takes

   quietly re-flows the 412px phones to a ragged 10+10+7. Three even rows of nine
   is worth more than 2px, and the width was never what made these look heavy. */
/* padding:0, not 5px 0 (the owner, 6 Nov 2026 -- the letters sat on the floor of
   their boxes on a phone). These chips are 24px tall with box-sizing:border-box and
   line-height:22px, both from browse_styles.php, so vertical padding cannot make one
   any taller: it only shrinks the 22px content box to 12px while the line box stays
   22px, and the letter drops out of the bottom of it. Measured on a 390px viewport,
   before and after: 11px of space above the glyph and 1px below, against 6px and 6px.
   The 24px height is untouched, so the tap target the rule was written for is too --
   the padding was never what provided it. No line-height here on purpose: the 22px
   comes from browse_styles.php and a second copy would only drift from it. */
#crb .crb-chip-l{width:37px !important;padding:0 !important;
	font-size:11px !important;margin-right:3px !important}

/* The two rows browse_head.php marked as open-on-desktop, folded here. This is
   the only place that knows the device, so it is where the decision lands.

   No !important: crbFold() opens a row by setting display:block inline, and an
   !important rule would outrank that and leave the tap doing nothing. */
#crb .crb-frow-mfold .crb-fset{display:none}

/* The markup's caret still points down until the script at the foot of
   browse_head.php runs. Rotating the glyph already there costs no reflow and
   keeps it from being wrong for those few milliseconds; once that script drops
   crb-flab-open the rule stops matching, and by then the glyph is right. */
/* crb-mpre, not crb-frow-mfold: the row keeps crb-frow-mfold for good (it is what
   folds the set), so keying off it rotated the caret of any row the visitor later
   opened as well. The script removes crb-mpre, so this only ever applies before it
   has run. */
#crb .crb-mpre .crb-flab-open .crb-caret{display:inline-block;
	transform:rotate(-90deg)}

/* THE FILTER BLOCK AS ONE ROW OF PILLS (the owner, 6 Nov 2026).

   Letter, Genre and Region were three full-width labelled rows stacked under the
   Top ROMs chip: a 160px filter block between the heading and the featured games,
   the same 160px at every phone width. They are pills on the Top ROMs line now and
   the block is 39px -- 121px of screen back, above the fold.

   display:contents on the rows rather than a rewrite of the markup: the label and
   its set become children of the flex container while staying put in the DOM, which
   is what crbFold() needs -- it finds the set with el.nextSibling. order is what
   keeps the layout stable: every pill is order 1 and every set order 2, so an opened
   set lands on its own full-width line BELOW the whole row rather than splitting it
   where that pill happens to sit. */
#crb .crb-filters{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:center}
#crb .crb-frow,#crb .crb-frow-top{display:contents}
#crb .crb-fset{order:2;flex:0 0 100%;margin-top:5px}

/* The pill. It was built to match .crb-chip exactly; since the chips lost their fill
   (see the note in browse_styles.php) it keeps one, and that is now doing useful
   work rather than being a copy: a filled pill above unfilled chips says which is
   the control and which are the options. Same border, radius, type and margins
   otherwise, because the row still has to read as one set of controls beside Top
   ROMs. text-transform:none for the same reason; uppercase set these apart from
   Top ROMs and cost about 15px a pill, which is the difference between one line
   and two on a 320px screen.

   a.crb-flab in the selector: browse_styles.php gives the anchor padding:6px 0 and a
   -6px top margin for its tap target, at a higher specificity than .crb-flab. The
   pill has its own 24px height, so that offset has to go or it sits a row proud. */
#crb .crb-flab,#crb a.crb-flab{order:1;display:inline-block;
	background:rgba(86,133,196,.14);border:1px solid rgba(134,176,224,.42);
	border-radius:3px;color:#cfe0f2 !important;font:bold 11px Verdana,Arial !important;
	text-transform:none;letter-spacing:0;white-space:nowrap;

.navbar .dropdown{position:relative;display:inline-block;vertical-align:baseline}
.navbar .dropbtn{background:none;border:0;padding:0;margin:0;color:#fff;
	cursor:pointer;line-height:inherit}
.navbar .dropdown:hover .dropbtn,.navbar .dropdown.cr-open .dropbtn{color:#dce9f7}

/* top:100% rather than a fixed offset, so the panel sits under the button
   whatever the nav row's height works out to in a given language. */
/* The bar's own blue, so the panel reads as the bar carrying on downwards
   rather than as a separate box dropped on top of it. The borders are
   black and white at low alpha instead of fixed colours: they then work
   as a shaded edge against whatever this blue is, and still would if the
   bar were ever retoned. The hairline along the top is the only thing
   marking where the bar stops -- a fold, not a break.

   No padding. The rows run the full width of the panel and sit flush
   against the border, so the hover fills its column edge to edge the way
   a native menu does, rather than floating in a blue margin. The items
   keep their own 5px 13px, which is what stops the text touching. */
/* white-space:nowrap is load-bearing, not cosmetic. The panel is absolutely
   positioned inside .dropdown, which is only as wide as its button, so the
   browser sizes it shrink-to-fit against that tiny available width -- and
   without this it picks min-content and stacks the three columns vertically
   in a 151px strip. nowrap makes the columns one unbreakable line, so
   shrink-to-fit resolves to the sum of them. */
.navbar .dropdown-content{display:none;position:absolute;left:0;top:100%;
	z-index:40;background:#4276bc;border:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.28);
	border-top:1px solid rgba(255,255,255,.22);
	box-shadow:0 10px 28px rgba(0,0,0,.55);
	padding:0;text-align:left;white-space:nowrap}

/* .cr-open is the touch path -- see the script under the nav. Hover alone
   left both menus unopenable on a phone or a tablet. */
/* grid, not block: grid-auto-columns:1fr makes every column the width of the
   widest one, so the row separators are all the same length. Left as
   inline-blocks each column shrank to its own longest label -- 119, 136 and
   149px for the ROM menu -- and the separator under "CPS1" was visibly
   shorter than the one under "Sony Playstation 3". The panel still sizes to
   its contents; 1fr equalises within that rather than stretching it. */
/* width:max-content is what makes 1fr equalise. Left to shrink-to-fit the
   browser sizes each fr track to its own max-content -- measured at 119,
   136 and 149px for the ROM menu -- and the separators came out three
   different lengths. Under max-content all three resolve to the widest,
   and the panel is still sized to its contents rather than to a pixel
   figure guessed for English. A browser too old for max-content falls back
   to auto, which is the ragged version: narrower, not broken. */
.navbar .dropdown:hover .dropdown-content,
.navbar .dropdown.cr-open .dropdown-content{display:grid;
	grid-auto-flow:column;grid-auto-columns:1fr;
	width:-webkit-max-content;width:-moz-max-content;width:max-content}

/* Three columns for ROMs, two for the shorter emulators list. cr_menu_panel()
   cuts them in PHP and emits one .crn-col each -- see the note there for why
   this is not column-count.

   No width on the panel: each column shrinks to its own longest label and the
   panel is the sum of them, so it is exactly as wide as it needs to be in
   every language rather than a number guessed for English. */
.navbar .crn-col{display:inline-block;vertical-align:top}

/* The rule between columns. One line on the column itself rather than a
   border on every item: the columns are grid children and stretch to the
   full row height, so it runs the whole depth of the panel instead of
   stopping where the shortest column runs out. That is what stops the
   leftover space at the foot of the last column reading as a hole -- the
   column is still clearly there, it just has no more entries in it. */
.navbar .crn-col + .crn-col{border-left:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.20)}

/* White, like the bar's own links, and normal weight: these are a list to
   scan, and at bold 13px the panel reads as 32 headings. White on this blue
   measures 3.79:1, which is exactly what the nav bar's own labels have
   always measured -- the panel is no harder to read than the bar it comes
   out of. Darkening the panel one shade reaches 4.47:1 if that is ever
   wanted, at the cost of it no longer being the same colour as the bar. */
/* border is set here, not left to css/style.css. That file puts a box round
   every item, which turned the panel into a grid -- and a grid with a short
   last column reads as cells that failed to load. A row separator says the
   same thing without implying a cell that ought to be filled.

   The separator stops at the foot of each column, which is only expressible
   because the columns are real elements. Under CSS columns :last-child meant
   the last item in the whole panel, so two of the three columns drew a line
   under nothing -- the thin trailing border. */
.navbar .dropdown-content a{display:block;font:normal 12px Verdana,Arial;
	color:#fff;padding:5px 13px;white-space:nowrap;text-decoration:none;
	border:0;border-bottom:1px solid rgba(0,0,0,.20)}

/* The group rule under the last platform entry: above it are the emulators that
   RUN ON a machine you own (Mac, Android, iOS), below it the consoles those
   emulators PRETEND TO BE. Two different senses of the word in one list, which
   is what the owner asked to pull apart (6 Nov 2026).

   White, where every other separator in the panel is black at 20%. The dark
   lines read as "next row"; this one has to read as "different kind of thing",
   and on this blue the only direction left is lighter. 2px for the same reason
   -- at 1px it is just another row separator in a different colour.

   Deliberately ABOVE the :last-child reset below, not after it. Both selectors
   score (0,3,1), so the later one wins a tie: if the platform entries happen to
   fill the first column exactly, this rule loses and no line is drawn. That is
   the wanted answer -- the column border already separates them there, and a
   rule at the foot of a column is the "line under nothing" the note above
   describes. */
.navbar .dropdown-content a.crn-sep{border-bottom:2px solid rgba(255,255,255,.65)}
/* The platform this visitor is actually on, bolded in the emulator menu (Ed, 21 Nov 2026). After the
   rule above and more specific than it, because the `font:` shorthand a few lines up sets weight to
   normal -- a bare font-weight placed before it would be overwritten. An entry can be both the last
   lead and the visitor's own, so the two classes have to be able to ride together. */
.navbar .dropdown-content a.crn-mine{font-weight:700}
.navbar .crn-col a:last-child{border-bottom:0}

/* A white wash rather than another colour: it lightens whatever blue is
   underneath, so the hover can never clash with the panel.

   45%, and the text inverts to black. Black on the result measures 10.8:1
   -- far clearer than anything white-on-blue can reach -- so the row the
   pointer is on is the most readable thing in the panel, which is the row
   you are about to click. A lighter wash than this leaves black looking
   muddy on a still-blue row; a heavier one turns the row white and reads
   as a tooltip rather than a selection. */
.navbar .dropdown-content a:hover{background:rgba(255,255,255,.45);color:#000}

   on this blue measures 1.2:1 -- invisible. So the red moves to the chip and
   the text goes white: 5.4:1 inside it.

   Red fill rather than a dark one. Nothing lighter than white reaches 4.5:1
   against this blue -- the arithmetic caps out at 3.79 -- so a chip that is
   going to read has to be dark, and a near-black one ends up the heaviest
   mark on the panel, which is backwards for a four-letter label. This chip is
   close to the panel in lightness and far from it in hue, so it reads as a
   red tag without punching a hole in the blue.

   Author CSS beats the presentational colour attribute, so the markup needs
   no edit. Swap the two colours below for the other treatments: #1f1f1f with
   #f2614a text is the dark chip, #fff with #c0392b text the white one. */

   actually hidden, so the desktop bar keeps its button and its deliberate click. The .js class is what

<script>
/* Tap to open, on top of hover.

   The menus were hover-only, and a touch screen has no hover: on a phone or
   a tablet neither of them could be opened at all. Tapping the button adds
   .cr-open, which the stylesheet above shows exactly as it shows :hover, so
   a mouse keeps the behaviour it had and nothing else changes.

   jQuery is already loaded in this <head>; this adds no request. */
jQuery(function($)
{
	var $menus = $('.navbar .dropdown');

	$('.navbar .dropbtn').on('click', function(e)
	{
		/* A <button> outside a form submits nothing, but the default is still
		   "submit" -- stop it rather than rely on that. */
		e.preventDefault();
		e.stopPropagation();

		var $d = $(this).closest('.dropdown');

		$menus.not($d).removeClass('cr-open');
		$d.toggleClass('cr-open');
	});

	/* Hover opens through CSS alone, which knows nothing about .cr-open. A menu
	   clicked open therefore stayed open while hovering the other one opened
	   that too, and the two panels overlapped. Entering either clears the sticky
	   state from the other. A tap fires no mouseenter on the menu you did not
	   touch, so the touch path is unaffected. */
	$menus.on('mouseenter', function()
	{
		$menus.not(this).removeClass('cr-open');
	});

	/* Anywhere else closes them, including a tap on the page behind. */
	$(document).on('click', function(e)
	{
		if(!$(e.target).closest('.navbar .dropdown').length)
			$menus.removeClass('cr-open');
	});

	$(document).on('keydown', function(e)
	{
		if(e.which === 27)
			$menus.removeClass('cr-open');
	});
});

#crp .crp-kv b,#crp .crp-kv .crp-k{color:#cfe0f2;font-weight:bold;margin-right:4px}
#crp .crp-kv a{color:#9fc0e0;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:2px}

/* --- /account.php: the account itself, one panel ------------------------- */
/* A .crp-kv each put four one-line boxes down the page, and four borders and
   four gaps for four short facts read as four separate things to deal with
   rather than as one account (Ed, 18 Nov 2026). One rectangle, hairlines
   between the rows.
   The left edge carries the plan's own colour -- account.php sets
   border-left-color inline, orange for premium and blue for basic, the same
   two the header greeting uses -- so which plan this is can be read off the
   page without finding the word. 3px is the width every other panel here
   uses for its left rule, so it lines up with them down the site. */
#crp .crp-acct{box-sizing:border-box;max-width:640px;margin:0 0 6px;
	background:#1b1b1b;border:1px solid #2a2a2a;border-left:3px solid #3a4150}
#crp .crp-acct .crp-row{font:12.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#b4b4b4;
	line-height:1.7;padding:10px 14px}
#crp .crp-acct .crp-row + .crp-row{border-top:1px solid #242424}
/* The labels in a column of their own, so the values line up with each other
   instead of starting wherever the word before them ended. Not a table: at
   phone width the value drops under its label and a table would not let it. */
/* padding-right, not min-width alone: min-width only holds the two apart while the label is NARROWER
   than it. "Username" and "Password" are not, so those two rows read "Usernameechang" (Ed, 19 Nov
   2026). The padding is a gap the label cannot eat into whatever it says. */
#crp .crp-acct .crp-k{display:inline-block;min-width:88px;padding-right:12px;
	color:#cfe0f2;font-weight:bold}
#crp .crp-acct a{color:#9fc0e0;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:2px}
#crp .crp-acct a:hover{color:#8ec0f0}
/* The quieter half of a row -- "(Manage subscription)" after the date. Greyer so the date stays the
   answer and the link stays an option, but the SAME SIZE as the row it sits in since 20 Nov 2026 (Ed):
   11.5px against 12.5px did not read as quieter, it read as a different kind of text, and the mismatch
   was the first thing the eye landed on. Colour carries the hierarchy perfectly well on its own. */
#crp .crp-acct .crp-sub{font-size:inherit;color:#8f8f8f;white-space:nowrap}
/* nowrap suits a label in brackets. It does not suit a sentence: on a phone it would push the panel
   sideways rather than let the note wrap under itself. */
#crp .crp-acct .crp-sub-wrap{white-space:normal}
/* The system and the date, under the ROM's name rather than beside it, and smaller (Ed, 20 Nov 2026).
   On one line they competed with the name for the row's width, and on a phone they wrapped anyway --
   badly, because the break fell wherever the width ran out rather than between the two things. Below
   it, the name owns its line and these two read as a caption, which is what they are. Not .crp-sub:
   that one takes the row's size on purpose, for "(Manage subscription)" sitting inside a sentence. */
#crp .crp-hsub{display:block;margin-top:3px;font:11.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#8f8f8f}
/* The date, right-aligned in a column of its own (Ed, 22 Nov 2026). It used to trail the system name after
   a middot, where it moved with the length of the name and nothing lined up down the list. */
/* Centred on the row, not floated to the top of it (Ed, 22 Nov 2026). A row is two lines -- the title and
   the system under it -- so a float put the date level with the title and left it looking hitched to the
   top. Absolute with the row as the containing block centres it against both lines at once, whatever the
   title does. padding-right on the row reserves the space, because an absolute element is out of flow and
   a long title would otherwise run straight under the date. */
#crp .crp-acct .crp-row{position:relative;padding-right:104px}
#crp .crp-hdate{position:absolute;right:14px;top:50%;transform:translateY(-50%);
	font:11.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#8f8f8f;white-space:nowrap}

/* Signing out. Sits under the account panel, spaced off it so it reads as an action taken on the panel
   rather than another line of it, and in the panel's own link blue. */
/* Signing out moved onto the username row (Ed, 22 Nov 2026), so .crp-out -- the block that used to sit under
   the panel -- is gone with it. Smaller and lighter than the value beside it on purpose: it is an action
   sitting in a column of facts, and at the same weight it would read as part of the username. */
#crp .crp-acct .crp-signout{font-size:11.5px;color:#9fc0e0;text-decoration:none;white-space:nowrap}
#crp .crp-acct .crp-signout:hover{color:#8ec0f0;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:2px}
/* The plan table's box. The same panel without a left rule: that edge means
   "this is your plan" directly above it, and a second coloured edge under a
   table that describes BOTH plans would be claiming one of them. */
#crp .crp-panel{box-sizing:border-box;max-width:640px;margin:0 0 6px;
	padding:6px 14px;background:#1b1b1b;border:1px solid #2a2a2a}

/* --- Sign in with Google ------------------------------------------------ */
/* White, because Google's branding guidelines say so and this is their mark on
   their button -- it is the one control on these pages that is not allowed to
   be themed to match the rest. The logo is their own asset at
   /images/google-g.svg; if the file is not there the <img> hides itself and
   the button reads as text rather than as a broken image.
   320px and centred (Ed, 18 Nov 2026), not the 640px column the form uses: at full width it read as
   another field rather than as a button. On a phone the cap is lifted again below, so it matches the
   submit button underneath it instead of sitting 40px narrower than everything else.
   Centred by .crp-gwrap and not by a margin of its own. Two earlier goes at this were both wrong, for
   the same underlying reason -- the element the button has to centre ON is not the element it is in:
     margin:0 auto   centres on #crp, which is the whole page width, so it landed 216px right.
     margin-left:160px  assumes the column IS 640. It is max-width:640, and inside the site's layout it
     comes out around 600, so the button sat ~19px right (Ed spotted it, 18 Nov 2026).
   The wrapper takes the same max-width:640 as .crp-form and .crp-or, so it is exactly as wide as they
   are whatever the column does, and justify-content does the centring against that measured width.
   260px as of 19 Nov 2026, down from 320. The label needs about 220 of that in Verdana Bold 13 plus
   the logo, its gap and the padding, so there is roughly 18px of air each side -- narrower than this
   and the text starts touching the edges on the signup page, whose label is the longer of the two. */
#crp .crp-google{display:flex;align-items:center;justify-content:center;gap:11px;
	/* width:100% matters now that this is a flex item: a flex item sizes to its CONTENT by default, so
	   without it the button shrank to the width of its own label (186px) and max-width never applied --
	   a max is a ceiling, not a width. 100% of .crp-gwrap, capped at 320. */
	box-sizing:border-box;width:100%;max-width:260px;margin:0;padding:11px 16px;
	background:#fff;border:1px solid #dadce0;border-radius:7px;
	font:bold 13px Verdana,Arial;color:#3c4043 !important;text-decoration:none !important}
#crp .crp-gwrap{display:flex;justify-content:center;box-sizing:border-box;max-width:640px;margin:0 0 4px}
#crp .crp-google:hover{background:#f6f8fa;border-color:#c9ced4}
#crp .crp-google img{display:block;flex:0 0 auto}

/* "or", with a rule either side. The spans are the gap: the lines are the
   pseudo-elements growing to fill whatever the word leaves. */
#crp .crp-or{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:12px;max-width:640px;
	margin:14px 0;font:11.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#a3a3a3}
#crp .crp-or:before,#crp .crp-or:after{content:"";flex:1 1 auto;height:1px;background:#4d4d4d}

/* --- /premium.php: the two plans --------------------------------------- */
/* Two cards on one row, stacking below about 520px -- flex-wrap and a 240px
   basis rather than a media query, because what decides it is whether two
   cards still fit, which is this container's width and not the window's.
   640px to match every other block on these pages: the plans, the comparison
   table under them and the questions under that all share one left and right
   edge down the page. */
#crp .crp-plans{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:14px;max-width:640px;margin:0 0 18px}
/* A column so the button can stretch to the card's width whatever it holds. */
#crp .crp-plan{flex:1 1 240px;box-sizing:border-box;position:relative;
	display:flex;flex-direction:column;
	background:#1b1b1b;border:1px solid #2a2a2a;border-top:3px solid #3a4150;
	padding:17px 18px 19px;text-align:center}
/* The longer plan, marked by the same orange the rest of the site uses for
   premium -- the top edge here, the greeting in the header, the download
   button a member gets. One colour means one thing throughout. */
#crp .crp-plan-best{border-top-color:#df9e59}
#crp .crp-plan-flag{position:absolute;top:-1px;right:-1px;padding:3px 9px;
	background:#df9e59;color:#241607;font:bold 9.5px Verdana,Arial;
	letter-spacing:.5px;text-transform:uppercase}
#crp .crp-plan-lab{font:11px Verdana,Arial;color:#969696;
	text-transform:uppercase;letter-spacing:.8px}
#crp .crp-plan-term{font:bold 20px Verdana,Arial;color:#fff;margin:5px 0 13px}
#crp .crp-plan-price{font:bold 29px Verdana,Arial;color:#df9e59;line-height:1}
#crp .crp-plan-each{font:11.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#939393;margin:7px 0 0}
/* align-self, because the card is a flex column: without it the badge is
   stretched to the card's full width and stops reading as a badge. */
#crp .crp-plan-save{display:inline-block;align-self:center;margin:12px 0 0;padding:4px 10px;
	border-radius:3px;background:rgba(91,199,122,.13);
	border:1px solid rgba(91,199,122,.42);font:bold 11px Verdana,Arial;color:#8fdca5}
/* The monthly plan saves nothing, so it has nothing to put here -- but it
   keeps the slot, empty and invisible, so both buy buttons sit at the same
   height. Two buy buttons a line apart, side by side, on the page where they
   are the only thing being asked for, is the first thing the eye catches. */
#crp .crp-plan-save-none{visibility:hidden}
/* The same gradient and border as the member's download button in
   includes/dl_offer.php (.cr-offer-gx), so the button they press to buy and
   the button they get for having bought are recognisably the same thing. */
#crp .crp-plan-buy{display:block;box-sizing:border-box;margin:15px 0 0;
	align-self:stretch;padding:12px 10px;border-radius:7px;
	background:linear-gradient(180deg,#d9903f 0%,#bd7020 52%,#a65f16 100%);
	border:1px solid #8a4e10;color:#fff !important;font:bold 13px Verdana,Arial;
	text-decoration:none !important;text-shadow:0 1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.35);
	box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.3) inset,0 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.4)}
#crp a.crp-plan-buy:hover{background:linear-gradient(180deg,#e8a04e 0%,#cd7f2c 52%,#b66c1d 100%)}
/* Nothing to press: no gradient, no shadow, and not a link. It keeps the
   button's size so the two cards stay the same height either way. */
#crp .crp-plan-off{background:none;border-color:#333;color:#8a8a8a !important;
	box-shadow:none;text-shadow:none;font-weight:normal;cursor:default}
#crp a.crp-plan-off:hover{background:none;border-color:#444;color:#b4b4b4 !important}

/* --- the tutorial's steps ----------------------------------------------- */

   with the title and the body underneath, so at a glance there was no way to

#crp .crp-step{position:relative;box-sizing:border-box;max-width:640px;
	padding:13px 15px 13px 54px;margin:0 0 8px;background:#1b1b1b;
	border:1px solid #2a2a2a;border-left:3px solid #4e97db}
#crp .crp-num{position:absolute;left:14px;top:12px;width:26px;height:26px;
	border-radius:50%;background:rgba(86,133,196,.2);border:1px solid rgba(134,176,224,.45);
	color:#cfe0f2;font:bold 12px/25px Verdana,Arial;text-align:center}
#crp .crp-step-t{display:block;font:bold 13px Verdana,Arial;color:#fff;margin:0 0 6px}
#crp .crp-step-b{font:12.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#b4b4b4;line-height:1.7}
#crp .crp-step-b a{color:#9fc0e0;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:2px}
#crp .crp-step-b a:hover{color:#8ec0f0}
#crp .crp-step-b b{color:#e4e4e4}

/* --- the FAQ contents list ---------------------------------------------- */
/* Numbered with a counter and list-style:none, like the rail's steps:
   browsers disagree about how much padding an <ol> marker gets. */
#crp .crp-toc{list-style:none;margin:0 0 8px;padding:0;counter-reset:crptoc;
	max-width:640px}
#crp .crp-toc li{counter-increment:crptoc;margin:0 0 2px}
#crp .crp-toc a{display:block;position:relative;padding:10px 14px 10px 40px;

	font:12.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#cfe0f2;line-height:1.4}
#crp .crp-toc a::before{content:counter(crptoc);position:absolute;left:15px;top:10px;

/* --- the FAQ entries ---------------------------------------------------- */
#crp .crp-qa{max-width:640px;margin:0 0 4px;padding:0 0 16px;
	border-bottom:1px solid #242424}
#crp .crp-qa:last-child{border-bottom:0}
#crp .crp-q{display:block;font:bold 13.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#fff;

#crp .crp-top:hover{color:#9fc0e0}

/* --- the contact form --------------------------------------------------- */
/* form.php used to be a page of its own with the same chrome around it. It is
   the bottom half of /contact.php now: the guidelines and the form they
   qualify you for were never two separate errands. */
/* /form.php redirects to this anchor, and a rejected submission comes back to
   it, so give it a little air above rather than landing flush to the edge. */
#crp #contact-form{scroll-margin-top:14px}
#crp .crp-form{box-sizing:border-box;max-width:640px;background:#1b1b1b;
	border:1px solid #2a2a2a;padding:16px;margin:0 0 16px}
/* Label beside the box, not above it (Ed, 18 Nov 2026). Register asks four questions now and stacked labels
   made it eight rows deep; on one line the form is half the height and the boxes line up in a column the eye
   can run down.
   A wrapping flex row rather than a table or a float: the label and the box sit on line one, and a hint takes
   the full width of line two and is pushed across by the label's own width, so it reads as belonging to the
   box rather than to the label.
   152px, and the number comes from Verdana's OWN advance widths rather than from anything rendered here
   (Ed, 18 Nov 2026). Measuring it in this project's container is worthless for this: Verdana is not
   installed there, so Chromium substitutes Liberation Sans and reports 111px for a label that Verdana draws
   at 126 -- which is how 128 and then 136 both shipped still wrapping. Summed from the font's metrics at bold
   12.5px, the widest labels are "Email or Username" at 132px and "Confirm Password" at 126; 132 + the 12px
   right padding is 144, so 152 leaves 8px of slack for hinting. A longer label in another language still
   wraps inside its own column rather than shoving the box sideways.
   align-items:flex-start, not center: contact.php's message box is 132px tall and a vertically centred label
   beside it floats in the middle of nowhere. The label's own padding-top is what lines its text up with the
   first line of text inside the box. */
#crp .crp-field{display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;align-items:flex-start;margin:0 0 15px}
#crp .crp-field:last-of-type{margin-bottom:12px}
#crp .crp-flab{flex:0 0 152px;box-sizing:border-box;padding:8px 12px 0 0;
	font:bold 12.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#cfe0f2;margin:0;line-height:1.35}
#crp .crp-req{color:#d98c3a;font-weight:normal;font-size:11px;margin-left:6px}
/* The way out of a forgotten password, on the password label's own row and hard right (Ed, 18 Nov 2026).
   Hidden on a desktop, where the label sits in a 152px column beside the box and there is no "far right"
   to put it at -- there the standalone link below the form keeps its place. One of the two is always
   showing and never both, so the page has a single link to that page whichever width it is read at. */
#crp .crp-forgot{display:none;font:11.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#9fc0e0;
	text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:2px}
#crp .crp-forgot:hover{color:#8ec0f0}

/* password joins text and email here (Ed, 17 Nov 2026, for /login.php and /register.php). It is a typed
   selector list, so a type the list does not name falls back to the browser's own control -- a white box on a
   dark form -- rather than inheriting anything. That is why it has to be added rather than assumed. */
/* flex:1 1 200px, so the box takes the rest of the row and drops under the label only when 200px will not
   fit beside it -- which is what makes the phone layout below mostly unnecessary. */
#crp .crp-form input[type=text],
#crp .crp-form input[type=email],
#crp .crp-form input[type=password],
#crp .crp-form textarea{display:block;flex:1 1 200px;min-width:0;width:auto;box-sizing:border-box;
	/* 7px top and bottom, down from 9 (Ed, 18 Nov 2026): four rows of 39px boxes made the form taller than
	   it needed to be. 35px still clears the 24px minimum a finger wants, and the label's padding-top above
	   is 8px to match -- one border plus seven of padding is where the text inside the box starts. */
	background:#141414;border:1px solid #2f2f2f;padding:7px 10px;
	font:12.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#e4e4e4;line-height:1.5}
#crp .crp-form textarea{min-height:132px;resize:vertical}
#crp .crp-form input[type=text]:focus,
#crp .crp-form input[type=email]:focus,
#crp .crp-form input[type=password]:focus,
#crp .crp-form textarea:focus{border-color:#4e97db;outline:0}
/* The rule under a field -- what a username may contain, how long a password has to be. Grey and small so it
   reads as guidance rather than as a second label, and sized off the input it follows, not the label above it. */
/* Full width of the next line, indented past the label so it sits under the BOX it describes. Without the
   flex-basis it would try to share line one with the label and the input. */
#crp .crp-hint{flex:1 1 100%;box-sizing:border-box;padding-left:152px;
	font:11px Verdana,Arial;color:#8f8f8f;line-height:1.45;margin:6px 0 0}
/* The field that failed validation, so the message at the top has something to
   point at. Typed selectors here on purpose: the input rules above carry a
   type selector too, and without one these lose the border-color to them. */
#crp .crp-form input.crp-bad,
#crp .crp-form textarea.crp-bad{border-color:#a05252;background:#1a1414}

#crp .crp-cap{margin:0 0 14px}
/* Lined up with the boxes rather than with the labels: the button is the end of that column, not a fifth
   question. Margin and not a flex row, because it is a child of .crp-form and has no label beside it. */
#crp .crp-form input[type=submit]{margin-left:152px;margin-top:8px;display:inline-block;
	box-sizing:border-box;text-align:center;
	min-width:200px;padding:13px 30px;border-radius:7px;cursor:pointer;
	background:linear-gradient(180deg,#8ec2f2 0%,#5a9ae0 52%,#4a8ad3 100%);
	border:1px solid #3f7cc0;color:#fff;font:bold 14px Verdana,Arial;
	text-shadow:0 1px 1px rgba(0,0,0,.35);
	box-shadow:0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.35) inset,0 2px 5px rgba(0,0,0,.4)}
#crp .crp-form input[type=submit]:hover{background:linear-gradient(180deg,#a2cef7 0%,#6aa8ea 52%,#5595dd 100%)}
/* The submit and whatever sits beside it -- on /user/login that is the way out of a forgotten password
   (Ed, 18 Nov 2026), to the right of the button rather than on a line of its own below the form. The row
   carries the 152px indent so the button still lines up with the boxes, and the button gives it up. */
#crp .crp-submit{display:flex;align-items:center;gap:16px;margin-left:152px}
#crp .crp-submit input[type=submit]{flex:0 0 auto;margin-left:0}
/* The link needs its own type and colour here. Everywhere else on these pages a link sits inside a
   .crp-p, which styles the <a> for it; out on its own beside the button it would otherwise render as
   the browser's default blue serif. */
#crp .crp-submit a{font:12.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#9fc0e0;
	text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:2px}
#crp .crp-submit a:hover{color:#8ec0f0}
/* A form that is nothing but a button -- the merge confirmation on /user/google. The panel's background
   and border exist to group a set of fields; around a single button they draw a box for no reason. */
#crp .crp-form.crp-bare{background:none;border:0;padding:0;margin:0 0 4px}
#crp .crp-form.crp-bare input[type=submit]{margin-left:0}

/* --- form messages ------------------------------------------------------ */
/* Same three rules the rest of the site uses: green reports a result, amber
   is a caution. Each carries a glyph as well, because colour alone is no use
   to anyone who cannot separate them. */
#crp .crp-msg{display:block;box-sizing:border-box;max-width:640px;background:#1b1b1b;
	border:1px solid #2a2a2a;border-left:3px solid #d98c3a;padding:13px 15px;
	margin:0 0 16px;font:12.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#b4b4b4;line-height:1.7}
#crp .crp-msg-ok{border-left-color:#5a9b5e}
/* A button that reads as a link. The resend on /account.php has to be a POST -- csrf_verify() checks a token
   and a link carries none -- but "send it again" is a sentence, not a call to action worth a 200px gradient
   button. A <button> keeps the form's semantics; this gives it the look of the <a> beside it. */
#crp .crp-linkbtn{display:inline;padding:0;margin:0;border:0;background:none;cursor:pointer;
	font:12.5px Verdana,Arial;color:#9fc0e0;text-decoration:underline;text-underline-offset:2px}
#crp .crp-linkbtn:hover{color:#8ec0f0}
/* Floated rather than inline: with a list of failures after it an inline glyph
   sits alone on a line of its own above them. Floated, it marks the first one
   and the rest clear it. */
#crp .crp-msg > svg{float:left;margin:3px 9px 0 0}
#crp .crp-msg ul{list-style:none;margin:0;padding:0;overflow:hidden}
#crp .crp-msg li{padding:0 0 0 16px;position:relative;line-height:1.7}

   is neither quiet nor clear, and it read as an empty slot rather than a control. The border is kept

   button stays 40x34, so a 24px glyph still has 5px of air above and below and the row height does not move. */

   last thing tapped until something else is tapped, so after closing a panel the button it was
   closed with kept its grey fill and read as still open. (hover:hover) is false on a phone, so the
   fill never applies there and the only fill the button ever shows there is the blue of being open.
   -webkit-tap-highlight-color kills the separate grey flash iOS paints over a tapped control. */

   around it light up when the search icon was tapped. The descendant selector costs nothing here -- it is a

/* 58dvh after 58vh, not instead of it (the owner, 6 Nov 2026). On iOS Safari a vh is

   rows sit under the floating bar with no way to reach them. dvh is the viewport as
   it is right now, address bar and all, and it reflows when the bar comes and goes.

   keeps the vh above, which is what it had before. */
/* 46 (Ed, 20 Nov 2026), and the number moved three times in one afternoon because the menu kept
   changing under it -- 62, then 48, then 54, now this. It is worth writing down what it is a function
   OF so the next change starts from the arithmetic rather than from a guess.

   316px of furniture, so the list stops at 339px on a 655px screen -- 52%.

   Analytics, 23 Oct - 19 Nov 2026) bottom out at 360x780, and those are SCREEN sizes -- a phone

#crmb-menu .crmb-list{background:#15202b;border-bottom:1px solid #6d99cf;
	max-height:46vh;max-height:46dvh;overflow-y:auto;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch}

   row, so it cannot wrap; fixed cells, so it cannot shrink below about 520px --

   It used to swipe: each ROW was its own scroll box, cells at 40% so two and a

   with no scrolling at all -- a card you have to find by swiping is a card most

   with min-width:0 makes them equal and lets them shrink below their content,
   which is the part a table cell will not do. 4px between them -- enough that the
   thumbnails do not touch, little enough that nothing is spent on gaps. From a

#crd .crd-rel,#crd .crd-rel > tbody{display:block}
#crd .crd-rel > tbody > tr{display:flex;gap:4px;white-space:normal}
#crd .crd-rel > tbody > tr > td{flex:1 1 0;min-width:0;width:auto !important;

#crd .crd-rel a{width:auto !important}

#crd .crd-rel > tbody > tr > td:not([colspan]) a{font-size:10px;line-height:12px}
/* 4:3 and the same crop as the desktop box (14 Nov 2026, the owner): height:auto showed the stored 260x226

#crd .crd-rel td img{width:100% !important;height:auto !important;

/* Desktop pulls this table one gutter to the left and makes it two gutters wider

   is a scroll box and the table is just a block, so that pull would shift the
   strip off the left of the screen and push the page sideways. */
#crd .crd-rel{margin-left:0 !important;width:auto !important;max-width:100% !important}

.crsh{width:auto !important;padding:7px 8px !important}

/* The blue button's speed line and its no-cap height used to live here, phone-only. They moved to

/* The interstitial. css/style.css gives #modal a flat width:480px, so on a 390px
   screen a quarter of it hung off the edge -- and it is centred with a transform,
   so the overflow was split either side and the close button went with it. */
/* The interstitial. Constraining #modal alone was not enough: it is centred with
   left:50% plus a -50% transform, so anything inside it that is wider than the box
   overhangs BOTH edges and gets clipped at each end -- which is why the body text
   was cut off on the left as well as the right. Pinning it to left:10px and taking
   the horizontal half of the transform off removes the centring entirely, and every

#modal-background{overflow-y:auto}
/* 95% of the viewport, not a flat 10px gutter either side (the owner, 7 Nov 2026). The old pinning

#modal .modal-header{padding-left:0 !important;padding-bottom:3px !important}

#modal .modal-header img{max-width:44% !important;height:auto}

/* Privacy Policy and Contact Us live in this blue bar on a phone too (the owner, 7 Nov 2026), on the SAME line as

   CoolROM.com link inside it, so each matches .footer{font-size:10pt} on its own

td.footer,td.footer a.footer{font-size:9px}

#crHero h1{font-size:23px !important}

#crHero .crHeroSys a{font:bold 11px Verdana,Arial !important;

#crHero input.crHeroGo{padding-left:12px !important;padding-right:12px !important;

	font-size:12px !important}
/* Featured games: all eight in one row that scrolls sideways. 104px cards put
   three on screen and leave about 45px of the fourth showing, which is the whole

#crb .crb-feat{overflow-x:auto;-webkit-overflow-scrolling:touch}

#crb .crb-feat .crb-cap{overflow-wrap:break-word;word-wrap:break-word}
#crb .crb-feat .crb-card img{width:120px !important;height:auto !important;

#crb .crb-toggle{white-space:nowrap}
/* "TOP 50 DOWNLOADED" / "TOP 50 RATED": 11px, up from 10, which is what the

#crb .crb-toggle a{padding:4px 8px !important;font-size:11px !important;

/* --- browse page: controls sized for a finger ----------------------
   Measured on a 390px screen before this block, every control on the page

   They are that size because the desktop sheet fits 27 letters across a

   The 24px height is untouched, so the tap target the rule was written for is too --

#crb .crb-chip-l{width:37px !important;padding:0 !important;
	font-size:11px !important;margin-right:3px !important}
